subsystems.name: Growth substrate
subsystems.role: provides a clean, crystalline template that guides boron atoms into a single-layer sheet.
parts: sputtering and annealing stage for cleaning

subsystems.name: Boron source
subsystems.role: supplies ultrapure boron atoms at a controlled rate.

subsystems.name: Ultra-high vacuum system
subsystems.role: keeps the surface free of oxygen and contamination during growth.

subsystems.name: Temperature control
subsystems.role: sets the substrate temperature, which selects the borophene phase and quality.

subsystems.name: Characterisation suite
subsystems.role: verifies the atomic structure and electronic properties of the grown sheet.

subsystems.name: Transfer and encapsulation
subsystems.role: moves borophene from the growth metal to a useful substrate without oxidation.
parts: protective coating such as hexagonal boron nitride

buildSteps.title: Clean the silver substrate
buildSteps.detail: A single-crystal Ag(111) surface is polished, then repeatedly sputtered with argon ions and annealed under ultra-high vacuum until it is atomically flat and free of contaminants.

buildSteps.title: Heat the substrate
buildSteps.detail: The clean silver is brought to an elevated temperature (typically several hundred degrees Celsius) to give deposited boron atoms enough energy to assemble into a crystalline sheet.

buildSteps.title: Evaporate boron
buildSteps.detail: High-purity boron is heated in an electron-beam evaporator or Knudsen cell until it sublimes, creating a slow, controlled flux of boron atoms that lands on the silver.

buildSteps.title: Grow the borophene layer
buildSteps.detail: Boron atoms self-assemble on the silver surface into a single atomic layer. The exact temperature and deposition rate determine which borophene phase forms and how uniform it is.

buildSteps.title: Cool and inspect
buildSteps.detail: The sample is cooled under vacuum and transferred to characterisation tools. Scanning tunnelling microscopy reveals the atomic lattice, while diffraction confirms its orientation.

buildSteps.title: Transfer to a target substrate
buildSteps.detail: A polymer film is spun onto the borophene, the silver is etched away, and the film is placed on the desired support (for example, an electrode or a chip) before the polymer is dissolved.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate
buildSteps.detail: Because borophene oxidises quickly in air, a thin protective layer such as hexagonal boron nitride or an inert polymer is deposited before the material is exposed to normal conditions.

prerequisites.tech: Ultra-high vacuum and molecular beam epitaxy
prerequisites.why: borophene only forms on an atomically clean metal surface, which requires pressures around 10^-10 millibar and precise atomic deposition.
the silver lattice acts as both template and catalyst; other substrates often yield disordered or oxidised boron.
scanning tunnelling microscopy and electron diffraction are needed to confirm that a single-layer boron sheet has actually formed.
techniques developed for graphene can be adapted, but borophene is far more reactive and easily damaged during transfer.
current methods produce only small flakes on costly single-crystal silver under vacuum, with no route yet to continuous, large-area sheets.

pathway.milestone: lab-scale growth of borophene on silver in ultra-high vacuum
pathway.unlocks: detailed study of its structure, strength and metallic conductivity.

pathway.milestone: growth on cheaper, more practical substrates such as copper or thin films
pathway.unlocks: lower-cost samples and larger domains for testing.
integration into electrodes, sensors and catalytic surfaces.
use in energy storage, catalysis and lightweight composites, if stability and cost are solved.
